findings.evidence: The required caption CAP-S4 'Issuing CA 1 verifies, then signs' renders as a tiny line pinned to the bottom-left corner. The plate is about x 20-130, y 475-487 at 960x540. That is about 3.3 px per character, which gives a cap height of roughly 4-5 px at 540p (about 9 px at 1080p; the minimum is 15 px at 540p and 30 px at 1080p). It is the only caption not centred at the bottom, and it is 3 to 4 times smaller than every other caption in the film. It stays in this state through the whole model hold for CAP-S4 (f871-f1050).
findings.why: Unreadable required caption (BLOCKER by definition). It also fails L-03, because the plate starts at x of about 20 px against a title-safe minimum of 48 px at 540p. The viewer gets no caption for the CA's verify-then-sign step.
findings.direction: Restore this caption to the standard size, the centred bottom position and the same plate as the other captions. Add a per-caption check of cap height and bounds so one caption cannot drift from the shared style.

findings.evidence: The caption plate is semi-transparent, so the 3D noise and grain behind it shows through the text. Glyph strokes break into hollow or sliced letters. 'The client validates the whole chain' reads roughly as 'The client vaudites the whole chain', and 'Different templates can use different issuing CAs' and 'Trusted RDP connection established' are similarly broken. In B-05.2 the plate is lightened by the pale desaturated flashback background. In B-02.1_b the orange channel bleeds through the plate behind 'needs a trusted'.
findings.why: The worst-case 8 px band around the glyphs includes this speckle and the bleed-through, so the effective contrast is below the 4.5:1 rule. Captions are legible only by guessing.
findings.direction: Make the caption plate opaque, or at least dense enough that scene and grain cannot reach the glyphs. Composite the caption layer after grain and DOF so the text has clean edges. Report the measured worst-case contrast per caption in the manifest.

findings.evidence: The must-read check labels sit behind or under other objects. 'Requester authenticated' is hidden under the 1SN0S Issuing CA 1 nameplate. 'Enroll permission granted' is overprinted by the white capsule ('Enro... mission granted'). 'Request meets template policy' is truncated by the signing press ('equest meets templ', 'templa policy'). In B-08.1 the note 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' overprints 'Request meets template policy' and runs off the right edge. The labels are also grainy and slanted away from the camera.
findings.why: Each check is a must-read label (L-06) that must be at least 90% unoccluded and facing the camera within 35 degrees during its beat. All four checks and the compressed note fail, so the viewer cannot read the four ADCS checks that this beat exists to show.
findings.direction: Lay out the check labels on a clear plane facing the camera, clear of the capsule, press and nameplate. Keep the nameplate out of the list area. Space the lines so they cannot overprint, and keep the 'name supplied in request' note on its own line.

findings.evidence: The six-check validation list is rendered as 3D text that is skewed far off the camera plane. It is huge in a, then collapses to about 5 px in b and c. Lines overprint each other and the chain cards ('Currently valid' crosses 'Name matches'). Tick icons are partly hidden behind the glyphs. 'Chain ends at a trusted root' is clipped at the right edge in a and in the strip. In B-06.5_a 'OCSP if deployed' is overprinted by 'Revocation OK' and reads 'JCSP if deployed'. For B-09.1 the web check labels are not visible in any of the three sampled frames. In the strip the list is clipped at the right edge ('Name matches port...', 'KU permits TLS s...').
findings.why: These are must-read labels for checks 1-6 and the web checks. They fail the 35 degree facing rule, the 90% unoccluded rule and L-03, and they cover the focal chain.
findings.direction: Keep the list on a camera-facing plane with fixed line spacing, inside the title-safe rectangle, and clear of the cards. Hold each label readable for at least 1.5 s. Put the OCSP tag on its own line below the list. For B-09.1 make the four compressed checks visible and readable.

findings.evidence: Behind the S2 caption 'The RDP server needs a trusted identity' (plate about x 292-668) a second, darker rectangle stays visible at about x 362-598, y 480-503. That is the exact footprint of the S1 'Secure RDP connection' plate. It persists for the whole S2 hold. A similar darker band appears under the S3 captions.
findings.why: A previous caption's plate still has alpha above 0 while the next caption is shown, so two caption layers are live at once (L-05 allows at most 1). It also breaks the 0.2 s clear gap between captions and adds a hard dark block under the glyphs.
findings.direction: Make each caption layer's alpha reach 0, with its plate, at its model vanish time. Verify frame by frame that exactly one caption layer has alpha above 0.

findings.evidence: In B-02.2 the must-read 'Unverified' tag overlaps the 'Self-signed' field in b. It is only about 5 px tall in the wide frame c. In B-02.3_c, B-03.1_a, B-04.1_b and B-04.1_c the 'RDPAuth' badge label sits behind the rdp01.1sn0s.lab plate and only a fragment is visible. In B-07.1 'WebServer-TLS' is hidden behind the WEB01 and portal.1sn0s.lab plates, which overlap each other. The 1SN0S.LAB plate is clipped at the top in B-04.1_b.
findings.why: 'Unverified' is the key message of B-02.2. The RDPAuth and WebServer-TLS names must be readable during B-02.3, B-04.1, B-07.1 and B-07.3 (L-06). They fail the unoccluded and size rules.
findings.direction: Stagger or offset the host plates so they never cover template badges. Give the Unverified tag camera-facing placement at least 18 px at 1080p, away from the card text. Keep AD and template labels fully inside the frame.

findings.evidence: The card fields must be read (SAN 'rdp01.1sn0s.lab', EKU 'Remote Desktop Authentication', and the web card's 'portal.1sn0s.lab' and 'Server Authentication'). They are rendered as free-floating text outside the card at about 6 px per character, so roughly 8 px cap height or less at 540p, and they shrink further in later frames. In B-04.5 the cabinet door covers part of them ('Remote ... top Authentication'). The flashback tag 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' is about 3-4 px high and 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony' about 7 px. In the strip both are bare white text over pale grey with no plate.
findings.why: Must-read labels need at least 9 px cap height at 540p (18 px at 1080p) throughout the moment they matter. The identity fields and the CA-request tag that distinguishes it from the RDP request cannot be read, and the tag cannot do its job.
findings.direction: Print the fields on the card face at or above the minimum size and hold the card to camera. Give the CA request tag and the flashback label a plate and a larger size. Keep them clear of other geometry.

findings.evidence: The must-read '1SN0S Root CA' nameplate has its plate buried in the plinth. All that shows is a thin black vertical bar in the middle of the text, between 'Root' and 'CA'. The white glyphs sit directly on gold, with a ghosted '1SN0S' beneath. White on the gold plinth is roughly 2:1.
findings.why: The root is the subject of B-05.1 and its name is a must-read label. It fails the 4.5:1 contrast rule and the 90% unoccluded rule.
findings.direction: Place the Root nameplate on a camera-facing plate with a dark opaque backing, fully in front of the plinth geometry, and keep it there for the whole beat.

findings.evidence: In B-09.3_b the title plate (about x 243-717, y 255-300 at 540p) lies across the Root plinth and the tops of the CA1 and CA2 vaults. The focal subject for that beat is ROOT_CA. In B-06.3 the AIA tags cover the certificate cards, which are the chain. In B-08.2_c and B-08.3_a the WEB01 label plate fills about 45-55% of the frame and covers the focal action (CERT-WEB stamping, then CERT-CA2).
findings.why: Text covers the focal subject's projected bounds, which L-05 forbids (0 frames). The in-world plates also swell to unreadable scale as the camera passes them.
findings.direction: Place the title in clear space or lower in the frame, away from the root, or compose the end shot so there is empty space for it. Cap the apparent size of in-world plates and move or fade a plate when the camera nears it.

findings.evidence: In-world text sits outside the title-safe rectangle (x 48-912, y 27-513 at 540p) or is cropped by the frame. The CLIENT01 plate is cut off on the left ('LIENT01', 'T01'). The WEB01 and 1SN0S.LAB plates touch the top edge. The AIA tag 'Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it' is clipped at the left ('issing intermediate?'). The check line 'Chain ends at a trusted ro' is cut at the right. 'LS not published he' is cut at the left, and the eligibility tags run off the top in B-07.3.
findings.why: Every in-world label that is on screen must lie inside the 90% title-safe area on every frame. These labels are partly or wholly outside it.
findings.direction: Position and size in-world labels so they stay inside the title-safe area, or fade or re-anchor them as the camera moves so they never cross the safe margin.

findings.evidence: The packet gives no palette-test frame, sampled role colours or CVD simulation results. The task description lists them, but manifest.json has none. By eye, the lit CA1 route is a pale desaturated cyan and the validated-green channel is a pale mint. They appear together in B-09.2 and differ mainly in thickness. The AD pillar (steel blue) stands next to the CA2 vault (violet) and the CA1 vault (cyan) in many frames. 'Amber' reads as salmon or coral.
findings.why: L-07 cannot be cleared, and the pale cyan and mint pair is the likeliest to fall below dE00 15 under deuteranopia or protanopia. Shape differs (trust link vs channel), which softens the risk.
findings.direction: Add the palette frame and the dE00 matrices for normal vision, deuteranopia and protanopia to the packet. Separate the cyan route and the validated green by lightness as well as hue.

findings.evidence: The standard captions measure about 9.7 px per character, which implies about 14 px cap height at 540p against a 15 px minimum. The title card is larger at about 11.9 px per character. The packet lists no measured cap height for any caption.
findings.why: The body captions are at or just under the L-01 floor. The size is estimated from the images, not measured.
findings.direction: Publish the measured cap height and the worst-case contrast for every caption in the manifest, and raise the body caption size slightly if the measurement is below 15 px at 540p.
